flags.title: Navajo Nation (San Juan County) — Most Isolated Territory in Continental US
flags.summary: The Utah portion of the Navajo Nation in San Juan County is one of the most isolated areas in the continental US. Limited broadband, healthcare, and legal services. Utah Navajo Health System: 435-678-3221. Navajo Nation Human Rights Commission: 928-871-7436. DNA People's Legal Services: 928-871-4151 / dnalegalservices.org.

flags.title: Ute Indian Tribe — Uintah and Ouray Reservation, Oil Revenue
flags.summary: The Ute Indian Tribe at the Uintah and Ouray Reservation has significant oil and gas revenue. Tribal services are well-funded but remote. Ute Indian Tribe: 435-722-5141 / utetribe.com. IHS Fort Duchesne: 435-722-6100.

flags.title: UADD 180-Day SOL with LGBTQ+ Protections — 2015 Compromise
flags.summary: Utah's Antidiscrimination and Religious Freedom Act (2015) is a unique compromise that added LGBTQ+ protections to state employment and housing law while also protecting religious organizations. UADD SOL is 180 days. Utah Labor Commission: 801-530-6801 / laborcommission.utah.gov.

flags.title: Salt Lake City Pacific Islander/Tongan/Somali Bantu Communities
flags.summary: Salt Lake City has one of the largest Tongan populations outside Tonga, plus significant Somali Bantu, Bhutanese, and other refugee communities. Language access is critical. Utah Refugee Services Office: 801-526-9524 / jobs.utah.gov/refugee. National Tongan American Society: 801-364-0723.

flags.title: Federal Minimum Wage — $7.25/hr, No State Supplement
flags.summary: Utah uses the federal minimum wage of $7.25/hr with no state supplement. This is the lowest wage floor in the registry. For wage claims: Utah Labor Commission: 801-530-6801 / laborcommission.utah.gov. Also file federal WHD.

flags.title: US Territory — limited federal program access
Involuntary Hold: Utah Emergency Admission
flags.message: UT involuntary psychiatric hold law: Utah Emergency Admission. Statutory authority: Utah Code § 62A-15-629. Maximum initial hold duration: 24 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 24 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in UT retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in UT: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Utah Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Utah Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
